text:
MASTER PROMPT (paste first)

Format: 16:9, 30 seconds, 24fps, 1080p. Cinematic 90s anime film look, hand-painted backgrounds, warm golden sunlight, saturated blue sky with cumulus clouds, soft film grain, gentle lens flare.

Setting: A seaside sidewalk in the afternoon. A tall chain-link fence runs along the right side, with the ocean behind it, palm trees, and an orange-lined road on the left.

Characters (use the attached sheets as strict references):

Mei Aihara (@Image1): wavy purple-black hair, round glasses, pink hoop earrings, pink and blue oversized sweater, green high-waist pants, white-pink-blue sneakers, black spiral notebook with stickers. Shy and bubbly.
Yuki Kageyama (@Image2): long white double braids, black blazer, turtleneck, slim pants, boots. Calm, observant, protective.
Luca Moretti (@Image3): messy blonde hair with a faded undercut, star face tattoos, neck and sleeve tattoos, ear piercings, white tank top, black trousers, leather shoes, cigarette in hand.

Sound style: Anime audio. Exaggerated sparkle chimes, soft “doki-doki” heartbeats, cute kyahaha laughs, wind and wave ambience, light lo-fi guitar under the first half, and a low tense string drone from 19s.

TIMELINE

0:00–3:00 | Luca, profile close-up
Camera: tight side-profile close-up on Luca, fence in sharp focus beside him, deep-focus background.

Action: He leans on the fence with the cigarette in his lips. Smoke drifts up toward the sky. In the soft-focus background, Mei and Yuki walk small and distant down the sidewalk. At 2:00 his eyes slide toward them and the frame blurs as the focus pulls away.
Sound: waves, seagulls, soft inhale and exhale, faint lo-fi guitar.
3:00–7:00 | The girls chatting (medium two-shot, eye level)

Camera: Front-facing two-shot at the same angle as the reference, with the fence and ocean at right, as they walk toward the camera.
Action: Mei gestures excitedly with one hand, clutching her notebook to her chest. Yuki listens with a small smile.

Mei (excited): “Gojo Satoru is so handsome, I could kiss and marry him!”
At 5:00 both burst out laughing. Mei closes her eyes and laughs wide-mouthed (her “cheerful laugh” expression). Yuki covers her mouth and laughs with a quiet “pfft”, shoulders shaking.
Sound: kyahaha! giggles, a cute sparkle “ting” on the punchline, and bouncy footsteps.
7:00–10:00 | The collision
Camera: Low ground-level shot of Luca’s black leather shoe stepping into frame while Mei’s sneakers drift past, slightly out of focus. Cut to a wide shot at the fence with the ocean behind them: Luca walks left to right, Mei walks right to left, looking at her phone-free hands, and they bump.

Mei (voice-over, still rambling, cut off): “I have his wallpapers plastered all over my room—”
Her notebook and books fly out of her arms.

Sound: shoe clack, quick “whoosh”, soft thump, “Eh?!” gasp, books slapping the pavement.
10:00–12:00 | Kneeling to pick up
Camera: Wide high-angle shot looking down at both of them crouching, books scattered on the sidewalk. Luca bends low and Mei crouches beside him, flustered.
Mei (flustered, soft): “A-ah, sorry!”

Sound: fabric rustle, shy breathing.
12:00–16:00 | Hands and eyes (the key shot)

12:00: Extreme close-up on the blue book. Her hand and his tattooed hand land on it at the same time.
Sound: all ambient sound drops out, one soft heartbeat “doki.”
13:00: Low-angle close two-shot over the book. Mei on the left with sunlit hair and glasses, Luca on the right looking down at her. Their eyes meet slowly. Her cheeks flush.

14:00: Extreme close-up on Mei’s eye. The pupil dilates and the glasses reflect sky and sparkle highlights.
14:45: Extreme close-up on Luca’s eye with the pierced eyebrow, face tattoos and a slight softening in his stare.

15:30: Return to the two-shot, slow push-in. Her lips part slightly.
Luca (low, calm): “...Here.”
Sound: double heartbeat “doki-doki”, a sparkle chime, soft strings. (Luca’s line is my addition, since the reference has no dialogue here. Remove it if you want it silent.)
16:00–19:00 | Yuki calls, Mei snubs him
Camera: Wide shot from behind Yuki’s position. Yuki stands on the sidewalk on the left, waving. Mei and Luca are kneeling at center-right with the fence behind them.
Yuki (calling out): “Meimei!”
Mei jolts, grabs her notebook and stands up fast. She does not look at Luca. She turns her head away, bows slightly without a word, and hurries toward Yuki with her head down. Luca stays crouched and watches her go.
Sound: gasp, quick footsteps, a “pip-pip” panicked blip.

19:00–22:30 | Yuki’s warning
Camera: Medium shot, low angle, over Yuki’s shoulder. Yuki grabs Mei by the arm, and both glance back toward the fence. Sun flare glints off Mei’s glasses.

Yuki (hushed, serious): “Meimei, that guy is with the Mafia. Be careful!”
Sound: the tense string drone rises, and the ambience gets muffled.
22:30–26:00 | Luca stares
Camera: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind Mei and Yuki (their heads blurred in the foreground). Rack focus onto Luca, who is now standing, hands at his sides, staring after them. A new cigarette smoulders and smoke drifts across the sky.

Sound: wind, a single low taiko or bass hit.
26:00–30:00 | Final beat

26:00: Close-up on Mei’s profile as she looks back over her shoulder. Their eyes meet one more time across the distance. She blushes and snaps her head away (the snub).
28:00: Cut to Luca. A slow, small smirk. He looks down at his tattooed hand that touched hers, then back at her fading figure.
29:00: Final wide shot. The fence, the ocean, smoke curling up, the two girls walking away small in the distance. Fade out.

Sound: a last “doki” heartbeat, a sparkle chime, then the music fades into waves.
Negative prompt

Realistic or 3D look, character design drift (wrong hair colour, missing glasses, missing face tattoos), extra fingers, text watermarks, camera shake, fast cuts during the eye-contact shots, western cartoon style.

text:
Create an EXTREMELY INTENSE, ultra-realistic, high-budget 30-second Korean action movie sequence featuring brutal, lightning-fast hand-to-hand combat inside a traditional Korean restaurant and its industrial kitchen.

 60 FPS, realistic motion physics, high-speed combat, occasional 120 FPS slow-motion impact shots, seamless camera tracking, explosive sound design, authentic Korean dialogue.

ACTION INTENSITY: 10/10 — MAXIMUM.
The sequence must feel like a combination of elite Korean martial-arts choreography, gritty street fighting, and an explosive blockbuster action climax. Every second must contain suspense, danger, movement, or a powerful cinematic moment.

MAIN FEMALE CHARACTER — IDENTITY LOCK @[Image 1](image_1)
A beautiful, athletic, 24-year-old Korean woman with a short, chin-length pastel-pink bob haircut, soft feathered layers, expressive dark eyes, natural Korean facial features, and a lean, powerful physique.

Her pastel-pink hair must remain clearly visible throughout the action, even under dramatic lighting.
Personality: Initially quiet, gentle, and respectful. When threatened, her expression transforms into an intimidating, ice-cold stare. Her fighting style is explosive, precise, aggressive, and extraordinarily fast.
Maintain identical facial features, pastel-pink hair, costume, proportions, and hairstyle across every shot.

ENVIRONMENT
A busy traditional Korean restaurant at night, transitioning into a cramped industrial kitchen.
Warm amber restaurant lighting contrasts with cold fluorescent kitchen lights. Stainless-steel counters, steaming pots, metal shelves, swinging kitchen doors, hanging utensils, stacks of plates, wet tiled floors, and narrow cooking aisles create a dangerous, highly interactive combat environment.

Steam bursts from boiling pots. Metallic objects crash to the floor. Glass shatters. Overturned furniture and scattered ingredients intensify the chaos.

SECOND-BY-SECOND ACTION SEQUENCE

00:00–00:03 — THE THREAT
Extreme cinematic close-up of a ruthless Korean crime boss slamming his palm against a restaurant table.
BANG.
An elderly restaurant owner flinches in terror.
Three muscular bodyguards in black suits stand behind the boss.
The crime boss grabs the elderly man's collar and threatens him in Korean.
Camera whip-pans toward a young pastel-pink-haired waitress standing motionless beside the kitchen entrance.
She slowly places her serving tray on the counter.
Her eyes narrow.
The restaurant becomes terrifyingly silent.
00:03–00:06 — THE FIRST EXPLOSION
One bodyguard aggressively approaches the waitress and reaches for her collar.
WITHOUT WARNING—
She explodes into motion.
A lightning-fast wrist deflection.
A vicious elbow strike into his padded upper torso.
She grabs his jacket, pivots, and slams him backward onto an empty restaurant table.
CRAAAAASH.
Plates bounce, chopsticks scatter, and the table collapses.
The camera rushes forward in a violent handheld tracking shot.
A second bodyguard charges.
She ducks beneath his punch and drives a powerful spinning kick into his chest.
He stumbles through the swinging kitchen doors.
00:06–00:10 — KITCHEN WARFARE
The camera follows the waitress directly into the industrial kitchen in one seamless tracking movement.
Two attackers rush her from opposite directions.
She slides beneath the first man's swinging arm, plants one hand on a stainless-steel counter, and delivers a powerful sideways kick that sends him stumbling into stacked metal trays.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The second attacker lunges from behind.
She turns sharply, catches his forearm, and uses his momentum to throw him across a preparation counter.
Metal bowls scatter across the floor.
Steam erupts from a nearby cooking station.
The camera circles rapidly around her as she moves through the chaos.
00:10–00:14 — THE STEAM ATTACK
A massive cloud of white steam fills the narrow kitchen aisle.
Visibility drops.
A muscular attacker suddenly emerges from the steam, swinging a heavy metal serving tray toward her.
She ducks at the final instant.
WHOOSH.
The tray smashes into a hanging rack behind her.
She immediately counters with three lightning-fast movements:
A palm strike.
A spinning elbow.
A powerful jumping knee into the attacker's guarded torso.
He crashes backward against a stainless-steel refrigerator.
BOOOOM.
The camera briefly enters dramatic slow motion, capturing her pastel-pink hair whipping through the steam.
Then instantly SNAP BACK TO REAL TIME.
00:14–00:18 — THE RELENTLESS COMBO
Two remaining attackers charge simultaneously.
The waitress leaps onto a low kitchen platform, launches herself forward, and performs a spectacular cinematic flying kick against the first attacker.
She lands, immediately pivots, and blocks the second man's punch.
A rapid-fire exchange follows:
BLOCK — ELBOW — DUCK — SPIN — KICK.
Five perfectly choreographed movements in two seconds.
The camera follows every strike with aggressive whip-pans and realistic impact shake.
One attacker crashes into stacked plastic crates.
The other tumbles across a stainless-steel counter, scattering vegetables and utensils.
The entire kitchen erupts in metallic noise.
00:18–00:22 — THE BIGGEST IMPACT
The largest bodyguard emerges through the steam.
He is nearly twice her size.
He charges with enormous force.
She dodges his first punch.
The second punch narrowly misses her face.
EXTREME CLOSE-UP: Her pastel-pink hair moves across her eyes.
She grips the edge of the counter, swings her legs upward, and executes a devastating cinematic double-leg push kick against his upper body.
120 FPS SLOW MOTION.
The attacker flies backward a short, physically believable distance and crashes through the swinging kitchen doors.
CRAAAAASH.
The doors slam against the walls.
A shower of loose utensils falls from a nearby shelf.
Cut instantly to real-time speed.
00:22–00:26 — THE FINAL BOSS
The crime boss stands in the restaurant doorway, stunned.
All his bodyguards are defeated.
He angrily removes his suit jacket and charges toward her.
The waitress remains completely motionless.
At the last second, she steps sideways, redirects his arm, and delivers a stunning spinning back kick.
BOOOOM.
He crashes backward into an empty dining chair, which collapses beneath him.
The camera pushes into an extreme close-up of her cold, emotionless face.
Her breathing remains controlled.
00:26–00:30 — THE SHOCKING REVEAL
The kitchen falls silent.
Steam drifts slowly through the air.
The crime boss looks up at her in disbelief.
He recognizes her.
His expression changes from anger to absolute terror.
He whispers in Korean:
"설마... 너였어?"
("No way... it was you?")
The waitress slowly removes her burgundy apron and drops it onto the floor.
CLOSE-UP: Her fearless eyes beneath her pastel-pink hair.
She replies in a quiet, intimidating Korean voice:
"이제 끝이야."
("It's over now.")
FINAL SHOT: A dramatic low-angle hero shot as she walks toward the camera through the steam-filled kitchen.
Massive cinematic bass drop.
HARD CUT TO BLACK.
CINEMATOGRAPHY
Extremely fast, aggressive Korean action cinematography.
Continuous handheld tracking during combat.
Rapid whip-pans synchronized with strikes.
Extreme close-ups of eyes, fists, feet, and facial reactions.
Dynamic low-angle shots emphasizing powerful kicks.
120 FPS slow motion ONLY for the most spectacular impacts.
Immediate speed ramp back into real-time combat.
Realistic body momentum, grounded stunts, and believable collisions.
Seamless camera movement through swinging doors and tight kitchen aisles.
Natural motion blur and dramatic depth of field.
SOUND DESIGN
Explosive Korean cinematic percussion, aggressive bass pulses, rapid heartbeat-like rhythms, deep impact booms, sharp whooshes, metal tray crashes, shattering dishes, steam hissing, footsteps scraping wet tiles, heavy breathing, and realistic combat grunts.
Music intensifies throughout the fight, then cuts into complete silence before the final dialogue.
NEGATIVE PROMPT
No cartoon physics, no exaggerated superhero powers, no floating characters, no unnatural body movements, no disconnected punches, no random teleportation, no distorted faces, no extra limbs, no changing hairstyles, no costume inconsistencies, no excessive blood, no gore, no blurry action, no unrealistic object interactions, no slow or weak choreography, no unnecessary pauses.
FINAL DIRECTIVE: Every fight movement must feel powerful, dangerous, fast, and cinematic. Prioritize extraordinary choreography, realistic collisions, explosive kitchen destruction, perfect character consistency, and maximum Korean action-movie intensity.

text:
Create a 30-second video in 1920×1080, with the realism of an ordinary recording a boyfriend made of his girlfriend during a summer walk in Japan.

The small story:
They have no particular destination. She has just opened a can of fruit juice, and he starts recording without announcing it. Over the next half-minute, she gradually notices the camera, gets a little embarrassed, and begins including him in the moment. Their familiarity should come through in how she waits for him, looks at him, and closes the distance between them.

The woman:
A beautiful Japanese woman around 24 years old, with an approachable, individual face rather than a polished model appearance. Dark brown eyes, natural skin texture, light everyday makeup, and straight black hair loosely gathered in a low ponytail. A few short strands around her temples have escaped in the summer humidity.

She wears a faded navy cotton T-shirt, loose ivory trousers, comfortable gray sneakers, and a small rust-colored crossbody bag. A plain elastic hair tie is around one wrist. Keep her facial features, hair, outfit, bag, and proportions consistent in every shot.

Her expressions are understated and responsive. Sometimes she looks distracted or squints in the light. Her smile develops because of something between them, rather than appearing on cue.

The place:
A residential neighborhood in a regional Japanese city, near a narrow canal. Late afternoon in midsummer, with warm sunlight still reaching the upper parts of the houses.

Use ordinary local details: patched asphalt, short concrete bridges over the canal, metal railings warm from the sun, compact houses with tiled roofs, frosted entrance windows, outdoor air-conditioning units, bicycles tucked beside gates, and plants growing in mismatched pots. Utility wires cross the sky. A striped fabric awning hangs outside a closed shop farther down the street.

Avoid famous landmarks and postcard compositions. The location should feel like somewhere the couple already knows.

How the camera behaves:
The boyfriend holds a small consumer camera at his own eye or chest level. Most of the time he is beside her or only a step behind. The viewpoint should feel like her companion's attention, with no third-person shots of the couple.

Let framing respond to their interaction. When she suddenly looks at him, he may take a fraction of a second to correct the composition. When he laughs, the camera moves slightly. When they walk, his footsteps create a gentle, uneven rhythm.

Use ordinary consumer-camera rendering: restrained detail, modest dynamic range, occasional clipped highlights, a little shadow noise, and slight focus hesitation when she moves closer. Preserve natural skin color.

Keep the camera's attention on her face, gestures, and shared surroundings. Avoid fashion poses, body-scanning shots, elaborate camera moves, slow motion, or a glossy advertising finish.

Suggested edit — six short memories from the same walk:

0:00–0:05
She stands beside a low canal railing with a small, unbranded can of mandarin orange juice. The recording begins just as she finishes lifting the pull tab. She takes a sip, lowers the can, and notices that he is filming.

She looks directly at him with a briefly puzzled expression, then gives a small, amused smile, as though silently asking, “Really, you're filming this?”

Begin with a slightly loose frame that includes her hands and the canal, then let the boyfriend adjust it toward her face.

0:05–0:10
A cut to the two of them walking side by side along the narrow lane. She carries the can naturally in one hand.

She gets half a step ahead, realizes he has slowed down while filming, and turns back. Instead of posing, she waits with a mildly impatient but affectionate look. Once he catches up, she resumes walking beside him.

Her gaze should meet the person holding the camera, not an imaginary audience.

0:10–0:15
They pause near a house entrance where a small glass wind chime hangs beneath the eaves.

A breeze makes it ring. She glances upward and listens for a moment. Loose strands of hair move against her cheek; she brushes them aside with her free hand.

She notices him still watching her through the camera and suppresses a smile before looking back toward the wind chime.

Keep this moment quiet and unhurried.

0:15–0:20
On a short concrete bridge, she stops to look down at the canal. The camera first catches the rippling water, then tilts back toward her after she has already turned around.

She leans slightly toward him to see what he is recording. Her face briefly comes too close for the camera's focus, making her laugh softly and step back.

The laugh should feel like a shared interruption, with a small answering movement from the camera.

0:20–0:25
They rest beside the bridge in the shade. She is closer to the camera now, relaxed enough to stop paying attention to being filmed.

She takes another small sip of juice, then holds the can toward him as an offer. Leave the can clearly visible in the foreground, separate from her face.

He does not take it during the shot. She gives a tiny questioning lift of her eyebrows, then draws it back with an affectionate smile.

0:25–0:30
She steps toward him and gently touches his free forearm, inviting him to keep walking. Only a small, natural part of his arm may enter the lower edge of the frame.

As they start moving together, he lowers the camera. The view drifts from her smiling face to her bag, their moving shadows, and the sunlit pavement.

Let the last second settle on the overlapping shadows of two people walking close together. End with an ordinary recording stop, without a dramatic transition or title.

Sound:
Use the sound that would actually reach the camera microphone: cicadas, the juice can opening, a few footsteps, a wind chime, faint canal water, distant tires on the road, and their quiet laughter.

A single softly spoken Japanese remark such as “撮ってたの？” may occur when she first notices the camera, but speech is optional. Do not add explanatory dialogue.

No music, voiceover, or added dramatic sound effects.

Continuity and physical detail:
There is one juice can, carried by her throughout the sequence. Its color, size, opening, and remaining shape stay consistent. The crossbody strap stays on the same shoulder. Her ponytail remains tied.

Hands should hold objects with believable contact and weight. Walking speed, foot placement, shadows, and reflections must agree with the surroundings. Keep the canal, bridge, houses, sunlight direction, and summer weather coherent between cuts.

Emotional direction:
The viewer should feel that she knows and trusts the person behind the camera. Build that feeling through small changes in distance and attention: noticing him, waiting for him, leaning in, offering a drink, and asking him to walk beside her.

Let ordinary pauses remain. Her beauty is something her boyfriend happens to notice during their time together.

The finished video should feel like a personal memory he would keep because of the way she looked at him that afternoon.

text: Raw vertical 9:16 video recorded on a phone's front camera (not on screen), one continuous 30-second take with no cuts. Sadie, a young woman in her early 20s with long honey-blonde waves, light natural makeup, small gold hoop earrings and a cropped cream knit top, sits at a small marble table by a big sunny window in a busy brunch café. Behind Sadie: other tables of people talking, a counter with a glass pastry case, plants, staff moving about, chalkboards too far away to read. Around 9 s a waiter sets down two plates, a lemon ricotta pancakes and a plate of eggs on toast, plus two iced coffees in plain glasses. Around 15 s she turns the pancake plate toward the camera; around 20 s she cuts a bite, eats it and closes her eyes; around 26 s her sister's hand reaches in with a fork and steals a piece of pancake, and Sadie swats at it, laughing. There are narrow alleys between stacked, faded red, blue and yellow shipping containers, sun-bleached concrete, stalls with colorful canvas tarps and hanging paper lanterns, food carts, wooden crates and fish barrels, metal stairs and catwalks, corrugated metal walls, an open harbor basin of deep blue-green water with moored wooden fishing boats and floating pontoons, cranes on the docks in the background, and colorful painted shop signs made of abstract shapes, not letters. author: @azed_ai
text:
Create an ultra-photorealistic cinematic portrait video featuring one woman experiencing three powerful emotions in a continuous, uninterrupted performance: genuine happiness, heartbreaking sadness with visible crying, and explosive anger. Her emotional changes must feel psychologically believable, with natural spoken dialogue, accurate lip synchronization, subtle facial microexpressions, realistic tears, and expressive vocal delivery.

Environment: A minimalist portrait studio with a pure white background, soft diffused frontal lighting, delicate natural shadows, and no distracting objects.

Character: A woman in her early thirties with expressive brown eyes, natural facial features, softly styled dark hair, minimal makeup, and a modest black high-neck top. Her identity, hairstyle, clothing, and facial proportions remain completely consistent.

Visual Style: Ultra-photorealistic facial performance, visible skin pores, fine facial hairs, realistic muscle contractions, natural eye moisture, detailed tear formation, subtle lip trembling, authentic breathing, and physically accurate facial movement.

Camera Language: One continuous intimate close-up framing her face and shoulders. The camera performs an extremely slow forward push throughout the entire sequence, gradually moving closer to emphasize the emotional intensity. No cuts, no angle changes, no sudden camera movements.

Audio: Clear natural female dialogue with precise lip synchronization, emotional vocal changes, audible breathing, soft laughter, trembling speech, sobbing, and increasingly forceful angry delivery. No background music.

[00:00-00:06] HAPPINESS | Genuine Joy

Begin with the woman looking directly into the camera, her face relaxed and her eyes bright. A small, spontaneous smile appears at the corners of her lips, gradually spreading into a beautiful, genuine expression of happiness. Her cheeks lift, delicate smile lines develop around her eyes, and she releases a quiet, breathy laugh. Her shoulders relax as she leans almost imperceptibly toward the camera, appearing excited and emotionally overwhelmed by wonderful news.

She speaks in a warm, joyful voice, smiling naturally between words:

Dialogue: "I can't believe it... I'm so happy. This is everything I ever wanted!"

Her eyes sparkle with excitement, and she finishes the sentence with a soft laugh. Toward the end of the moment, her smile begins to weaken as an unexpected realization crosses her face.

[00:06-00:13] CRYING | Heartbreak

Her happiness gradually collapses into sadness. The smile disappears, her eyebrows lift toward the center, and her eyes begin filling with tears. She tries to maintain composure, pressing her trembling lips together while taking a shaky breath. Moisture gathers along her lower eyelids before the first tear spills over and slowly travels down her cheek.

Her breathing becomes uneven, her chin trembles, and she attempts to speak through the emotion. Her voice cracks naturally, interrupted by a small involuntary sob.

Dialogue: "But... you promised me. You said you'd never leave me..."

She struggles to finish the sentence, briefly lowering her gaze as another tear begins rolling down her opposite cheek. Her mouth trembles, her nostrils flare with a shaky inhale, and she closes her eyes momentarily as the pain becomes overwhelming. Her crying must feel authentic and restrained, with visible emotional effort rather than exaggerated theatrical sobbing.

[00:13-00:20] ANGER | Emotional Explosion

Her sadness gradually transforms into anger while the tears remain visible on her cheeks. She inhales sharply, raises her head, and fixes her eyes directly on the camera. Her eyebrows lower, her jaw tightens, and the trembling in her lips gradually becomes a firm, controlled expression. Her breathing changes from broken sobs into deeper, more forceful breaths.

She begins speaking through clenched teeth, her voice initially low and shaking with suppressed anger.

Dialogue: "You lied to me..."

She pauses briefly, swallowing her emotions as her eyes narrow and her facial muscles tense. Her voice suddenly rises with genuine fury.

Dialogue: "HOW COULD YOU DO THIS TO ME?!"

Her eyebrows pull together sharply, her nostrils flare, and her mouth opens naturally with the force of the final words. Her voice breaks slightly because she is still crying, creating a believable mixture of heartbreak and rage. She finishes the sentence breathing heavily, her jaw clenched, tears still visible, and her eyes locked intensely on the camera.

The final frame holds on her furious, tear-streaked face as she struggles to regain control.

Emotional Continuity: The performance must feel like one uninterrupted emotional experience. Happiness gradually gives way to heartbreak, and heartbreak intensifies into anger. Preserve overlapping emotional cues, particularly the transition from crying into rage, where tears continue flowing even as her facial expression becomes increasingly aggressive.

Facial Performance: Prioritize realistic facial anatomy, natural asymmetry, detailed eyebrow movement, subtle cheek tension, lower-lip trembling, involuntary blinking, eye moisture, visible tear accumulation, realistic tear trails, and physically accurate jaw movement during speech.

Dialogue and Lip Synchronization: Every spoken word must align precisely with her mouth movements. Her voice should evolve naturally from light, joyful warmth to fragile, trembling sadness and finally intense, emotionally strained anger. Include realistic pauses, breaths, vocal cracks, and changes in volume without making the dialogue sound theatrical or artificially generated.

Camera and Lighting: Maintain a single continuous close-up with a very slow push-in. Preserve identical facial proportions, hairstyle, clothing, white background, lighting direction, and skin texture throughout.

Negative Guidance: No identity changes, sudden emotional switching, exaggerated facial acting, cartoon expressions, artificial tears, frozen eyes, unnatural mouth movements, inaccurate lip synchronization, inconsistent tear positions, plastic skin, beauty filters, facial morphing, camera cuts, subtitles, text, logos, background music, or additional characters.

A quiet older Seoul neighborhood on a mild sunny afternoon.
Narrow residential lane, low brick houses, red-brick villas, potted plants by doorways, parked bicycles, utility poles with tangled overhead wires, mature trees.
A small neighborhood playground with a slide, a sandbox and a few low trees along a short fence.

CAMERA & LOOK
Raw handheld early-2000s DV camcorder footage.
Shaky hand movement, autofocus hunting, faded slightly cyan-tinted colors, exposure shifts between sun and shade, motion blur, soft standard-definition-like detail upscaled, occasional accidental zoom in and out, imperfect off-center framing.
The camera operator sometimes reacts a little late.

AUDIO
Natural neighborhood ambience recorded by the camcorder mic: birds, children playing in the distance, a bicycle bell, footsteps on asphalt, wind hitting the mic, faint distant traffic.
No music.

0–5s — LANE
She walks slowly through the quiet residential lane, shopping bag on her left shoulder, the camera following slightly behind and to her right.
Sunlight flickers through the trees.

5–10s — PLAYGROUND
She passes the small playground.
The camera accidentally zooms in and finds the little girl on tiptoe under a low tree branch, reaching up but unable to touch the red balloon caught in the leaves, its string dangling just out of reach.
The woman slows down, notices her, and walks over.

10–17s — FREEING THE BALLOON
Medium shot from the side.
Standing beside the girl, the woman reaches up with her right hand, gently untangles the string from the branch and pulls the red balloon down.
The string is clearly held in her right hand.
She bends down and places the string into the girl's small hand; the girl grips it tightly and the balloon floats above her head.

17–21s — THANK YOU
Same continuous shot, both of them in frame, the camera slightly off to the side.
The girl looks up holding the balloon and says brightly in English: "Thank you!"
The woman smiles and replies softly: "You're welcome."
The girl runs back toward the slide, still holding the balloon string, the red balloon bobbing above her.

21–26s — WALKING HOME
Cut.
The woman walks on down the lane, smiling to herself, bag on her left shoulder.
A light breeze moves loose strands of her hair, and a few dry leaves skitter across the street.
The camera follows a few steps behind, wobbling.

26–30s — HOME
She reaches the gate of a small red-brick house, opens it, then turns back toward the camera and says with a relaxed smile: "Pretty nice Sunday."
She steps inside and the gate swings shut.
Hard cut to black.

In the bedroom it jumps onto furniture and disturbs sleeping people. In the hallway it sends small objects tumbling. In the kitchen it knocks items off the counter. In the living room it darts across shelves and tips things over. In the garden it rustles plants, digs, or startles birds. On the fence it rattles loose objects. In the garage it weaves through clutter and causes things to wobble or fall. On the rooftop it skids across surfaces and startles other animals. In the tree it shakes branches and scatters leaves. In the street or alley it darts through trash, shadows, and unexpected little messes, always leaving brief chaos behind before sprinting onward.The cat behaves like a restless, curious nighttime troublemaker: climbing, leaping, squeezing through gaps, chasing tiny movements, staring at strange things, swatting objects, knocking things over, and vanishing into corners before bursting back out again. The overall feeling is funny, lively, mischievous, and cinematic, like a whole secret night of cat behavior compressed into one rapid continuous chase.

author: @AIwithSynthia
text:
SHOT 1 (0–6 seconds)**

A busy afternoon on a real Manhattan street. Yellow taxis are stuck bumper-to-bumper, delivery bikes weave through traffic, and pedestrians cross at the intersection. Inside a red Tesla Roadster, a young female delivery driver holds a Starbucks coffee securely in the cup holder. Her phone reads, “Customer waiting.”

She glances at the traffic, then at the clock, looking genuinely frustrated.

**Girl:** “Come on, come on… it's literally just one coffee!”

The camera feels like someone sitting in the passenger seat, casually recording her.

**Audio:** Real traffic, horns, turn signals, phone navigation, muffled city noise.

**SHOT 2 (6–12 seconds)**

She looks through the windshield. Traffic hasn't moved. She sighs, notices a small unfamiliar button on the dashboard marked “FLIGHT,” and stares at it for a second.

**Girl:** “You're kidding me.”

She presses it.

A low mechanical hum starts. The car vibrates slightly. A few pedestrians turn as the vehicle slowly rises above the road, kicking up dust, loose receipts, and water from the pavement.

A man standing beside a yellow taxi looks up.

**Man:** “Yo! Is that car flying?!”

Someone nearby immediately starts filming on their phone.

**SHOT 3 (12–19 seconds)**

A handheld street-level shot captures the Tesla moving above the traffic, not too fast. The car passes between Manhattan buildings, tilting slightly as it adjusts its balance. The camera operator struggles to keep it in frame.

Cut to a distant view of the car passing near the Empire State Building, then returning toward the street.

Inside the Tesla, the girl keeps one hand on the steering wheel and checks that the coffee hasn't spilled.

**Girl:** “Okay… this is actually working.”

Her phone navigation speaks casually.

**Phone voice:** “You have arrived at your destination.”

She looks down at the street below.

**Girl:** “I'M STILL SIX BLOCKS AWAY!”

**SHOT 4 (19–25 seconds)**

The Tesla descends toward a Manhattan apartment building. A customer leans out of an open window on a lower floor, looking confused. The car hovers just outside, maintaining a little distance from the building.

The driver lowers her window and holds out the Starbucks cup.

**Girl:** “Caramel latte for Jake?”

**Customer:** “You flew here for my coffee?”

**Girl:** “Parking was impossible.”

He takes the cup, examines it, and gives a small nod.

**Customer:** “Respect.”

**SHOT 5 (25–30 seconds)**

The girl gives a quick thumbs-up, rolls up the window, and the Tesla drops gently toward the street before accelerating away.

The customer takes a sip while watching the car disappear.

A passerby beside him calls out:

**Passerby:** “Hey! Can you order me one too?”

The customer looks at his coffee.

**Customer:** “Bro, I'm not sharing.”

Cut abruptly to black.

**Sound:** Natural city ambience throughout, with modest electric motor noise, real reactions, and no overpowering soundtrack.

**REALISM RULES:** Use ordinary New York street lighting and natural colors. Keep the actors' reactions understated and spontaneous. Avoid glowing blue trails, giant explosions, dramatic slow motion, perfect camera tracking, futuristic holograms, exaggerated facial expressions, and glossy CGI. The flying feature is fictional, but the footage should resemble real-world video with practical-looking effects. Maintain consistent vehicle design, realistic reflections, believable movement, and natural dialogue timing. No narrator, no robotic voices, no artificial-looking crowds.

Close-up of the feather in his hand. The surroundings dissolve into a flashback: the girl smiling at him beneath a streetlight, gently holding his hand. The memory begins breaking apart like fading ink on wet paper.

Scene 3 (10–15s — The Message):
Back in the present, he discovers a folded handwritten letter beneath the feather. His trembling fingers open it. As he reads, a tear falls onto the paper. The ink begins spreading across the page.

Scene 4 (15–20s — The Return):
A black swallow suddenly lands on the rooftop railing. The boy freezes. The bird looks directly at him, then transforms briefly into the girl's silhouette, her familiar faint smile appearing for just a moment.

Scene 5 (20–25s — One Last Moment):
He reaches toward her, but she turns back into the swallow. Instead of chasing her, he gently lowers his hand. The bird brushes past his fingers before taking flight.

Scene 6 (25–30s — Until We Meet Again):
The boy watches the swallow disappear into the cloudy night sky. He holds the letter against his chest and finally smiles through his tears. A flock of black swallows crosses the moonless sky. Camera slowly pulls away, leaving him standing beneath the rain. Fade to black.

author: @MayorKingAI
text:
SCENE CONTEXT
EXACTLY 4 HUMAN CHARACTERS — NO DUPLICATES, NO EXTRAS: the boss, the courier and two silent bodyguards, all Mexican. Interior, the back room of a closed cantina in Guadalajara, Mexico, late at night. A courier nicknamed Flaco reports to his boss that the merchandise is gone: a rival family, the Mendozas, ambushed his team on the highway to Tepic and took the whole load. The boss starts completely calm while he eats; the tension rises with every line; he explodes, then drops to a cold, lethal whisper. Crime drama, real time. Only the boss and the courier speak.

CHARACTERS
ERNESTO (the boss): heavyset Mexican man, slicked-back grey hair, thick grey moustache, a thin old scar cutting through his left eyebrow, heavy-lidded eyes. Black button-up shirt with subtle dark embroidery on the yoke, sleeves rolled to the forearm, a small sauce stain on the cuff, a thick gold chain at the neck. A worn gold signet ring on his right hand. 178 cm.
FLACO (the courier): very thin, wiry Mexican man, short black hair neatly cut, thin moustache, a small fresh bruise on his left cheekbone, a faded tattoo of a small cross on the back of his right hand. Clean, pressed white short-sleeved shirt, dark jeans, worn brown leather boots, a gold wristwatch with a freshly cracked face. He looks put-together, but his nerves betray him. 182 cm.
THE BODYGUARDS: two broad, silent men in plain dark short-sleeved shirts, one with a shaved head and a thick black beard, the other with a grey buzz cut and a crooked nose. They stand against the back wall in the half-dark, arms crossed, never speaking.

LOCATION MAP
A small square table with a worn green oilcloth sits at the center under a single hanging lamp, with a slow ceiling fan above it. Ernesto sits on the right side of the table (screen-right), facing left, with a plate of carne asada, a stack of warm corn tortillas in a cloth, a small clay bowl of salsa, a fork and a full shot glass of tequila. A box of dominoes rests at the edge of the table. An empty wooden chair waits on the left side of the table (screen-left). The two bodyguards stand against the back wall behind the table, one at the left third and one at the right third of the frame, partly in shadow. In the dark background: stacked beer crates without labels, a closed swinging kitchen door, a wall of painted talavera tiles, an old calendar, closed window blinds. The eyeline axis runs left–right across the table; the camera always stays on the same side of it.

FORMAT
One scene, 11 shots joined by clean hard cuts, classic shot–reverse-shot coverage. Cuts follow the dialogue and also land on the listener's reaction. The framing gets tighter and the silences longer as the tension rises, until the explosion in Shot 9. No fades, no dissolves, no split screens.

SHOTS
Shot 1 — Wide shot, locked-off, from the far corner of the room, 63° FOV. Ernesto eats in the pool of light while the ceiling fan turns slowly above him; the two bodyguards stand motionless against the back wall. Flaco walks in from screen-left and stops beside the empty chair, standing, hands at his sides. He does not sit. Ernesto keeps eating and ignores him.

Shot 2 — Medium close-up on Ernesto, 47° FOV, eye level, static. He tears a tortilla, keeps chewing, eyes on his plate. Without looking up, he points his fork at the empty chair. Relaxed, unhurried: "Siéntate, Flaco."

Shot 3 — Medium shot on Flaco, 47° FOV, static. Only now does Flaco pull out the chair and sit down slowly, on the front edge of the seat, back straight, hands resting stiffly on his knees.

Shot 4 — Medium close-up on Ernesto, 47° FOV, static. Still eating, still not looking at him. Casual, almost friendly, mouth half full: "¿Y? ¿Cómo salió lo de Tepic?"

Shot 5 — Reverse: medium close-up on Flaco over Ernesto's out-of-focus right shoulder, 47° FOV; one bodyguard is visible out of focus in the background. Flaco rubs his palms slowly along his thighs, swallows, his eyes flick from the plate to Ernesto's face. Fast and nervous, words tumbling out: "Los Mendoza nos cayeron en la carretera, patrón. Tres camionetas. Se llevaron la mercancía. Toda."

Shot 6 — Close-up on Ernesto, 29° FOV, static. His chewing slows… and stops. A long silence. For the first time he lifts his eyes to Flaco. No expression at all. Flat, quiet, slowly, as a statement: "Toda."

Shot 7 — Reverse close-up on Flaco, 29° FOV, handheld with an extremely subtle breath-like float. He cannot hold Ernesto's gaze; his eyes drop, then come back. His jaw tightens, his breathing becomes shallow, his fingers grip his knees. Voice cracking, pleading: "Nos agarraron por sorpresa. No pude hacer nada, patrón. Se lo juro."

Shot 8 — Extreme close-up insert on the table, 29° FOV, static. Ernesto sets his fork down beside the plate with a soft click. His hand rests flat on the oilcloth; his fingers slowly curl into a fist. Silence; only the creak of the ceiling fan.

Shot 9 — Medium shot on Ernesto, 47° FOV, handheld, the camera jolting once with the impact. He slams his open palm onto the table; the shot glass jumps and spills a little tequila, the dominoes box rattles. He leans over the table toward Flaco, veins visible on his neck, face red, shouting hard: "¡La quiero de vuelta! ¡Haz lo que tengas que hacer!" Behind him, both bodyguards uncross their arms and take one step forward.

Shot 10 — Close-up on Ernesto, 29° FOV, slow push-in ending on his eyes. Still leaning in, his breathing heavy, his face half in shadow under the lamp. His voice suddenly drops to a cold, quiet whisper, each word deliberate: "O no vuelves a ver salir el sol."

Shot 11 — Two-shot in profile across the table, 47° FOV, slow lateral drift of less than half a meter to the right, ending with both faces and the table between them in frame, the bodyguards out of focus behind. Ernesto slowly sits back, smooths his shirt, picks up the shot glass and drinks the tequila in one swallow. Flaco stays frozen in his chair, breathing hard, staring at him. Hold in silence.

CHARACTER ACTING
Naturalistic film acting with a steady, rising tension. Ernesto: total, unhurried calm in Shots 1–4 (he ignores Flaco, eats, never looks at him); the first eye contact in Shot 6 is the turning point; quiet tension in Shot 8; a sudden, real explosion of rage in Shot 9 (jaw clenched, eyes wide, neck tendons tight); then an instant return to icy control in Shot 10, which is the most frightening moment. Flaco: tension held inside the body — stiff posture, hands on his knees, rubbing his thighs, swallowing, quick eye movements, shallow breathing; he flinches back in his chair at the slam. His skin stays dry. The bodyguards stay expressionless and silent throughout. Faces show living micro-expressions and natural irregular blinks.

LIGHTING
One warm 3000K hanging lamp over the table is the key source: hard top light, fast falloff, deep shadows filling the room, eye sockets partly in shadow; the bodyguards are mostly in shadow, lit only on their shoulders and the edges of their faces. The slowly turning ceiling fan above the lamp casts soft rhythmic shadows across the table and faces; the lamp swings slightly after the slam in Shot 9. A faint red neon glow from the cantina sign outside leaks through the slats of the closed blinds in the background. Light color stays identical after every cut.

AUDIO
All dialogue in natural, clear Mexican Spanish with an authentic Mexican accent and intonation. Ernesto: deep voice, casual and slow at first, flat and quiet, then a loud raw shout in Shot 9, then a cold whisper in Shot 10. Flaco: tense tenor voice, fast and breathy, cracking when he pleads. The bodyguards never speak. Each speaker has a distinct voice. Only one person speaks at a time, no interruptions or overlapping, natural pauses between lines. Lip movements synchronized with the Spanish dialogue. Ambience: creaking ceiling fan, distant refrigerator hum, faint street traffic and a dog barking far away outside, fork against the plate, chewing, the chair scraping on the floor tiles in Shot 3, Flaco's breathing, a heavy palm slam on the table, the shot glass knocking on the wood. Ambience stays below the dialogue. No background music.

SUBTITLES
Burned-in English subtitles, bottom-center inside the title-safe area, positioned 8% above the bottom edge of the frame. White sans-serif text with a thin black outline, maximum two lines, stable position and size in every shot. Each subtitle appears and disappears exactly in sync with its spoken line:
Shot 2: "Sit down, Flaco."
Shot 4: "So? How did the Tepic job go?"
Shot 5: "The Mendozas hit us on the highway, boss. Three trucks. They took the merchandise. All of it."
Shot 6: "All of it."
Shot 7: "They caught us by surprise. I couldn't do anything, boss. I swear."
Shot 9: "I want it back! Do whatever you have to do!"
Shot 10: "Or you'll never see the sun rise again."
Subtitle spelling must match exactly. No other text on screen.

STYLE
Gritty Mexican crime drama. 35mm film texture with organic grain, light haze in the air, shallow depth of field, crushed blacks, soft halation around the lamp, no digital sharpening. Palette: 55% deep black and shadow, 30% warm amber and worn green, 15% red neon accent.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly four people for the entire scene: Ernesto, Flaco and two bodyguards. Same faces, hair, clothing, bruise, gold chain, watch and signet ring in every shot. Ernesto always screen-right looking left; Flaco always screen-left looking right; the bodyguards always against the back wall. Flaco stands in Shots 1 and 2 and sits down only in Shot 3, after Ernesto tells him to; from Shot 3 onward he stays seated. Exactly 7 spoken lines: 5 by Ernesto, 2 by Flaco. Ernesto stays seated; the bodyguards take only one step forward in Shot 9. Hands and fingers anatomically correct. Faces stable. The scene ends in silence with Ernesto drinking his tequila and Flaco frozen.

text:
リアルな実写の日本のショートドラマ。男性目線のPOV映像。
日本の大学近くの夜の帰り道。20代前半の日本人女子大学生と男性大学生が、肩を並べて同じ方向へ歩いている。
男性本人は映らず、カメラそのものが男性の視点。男性は女性より少し背が高い。女性は男性のすぐ隣を歩き、カメラとの距離は近め。
30秒間すべてワンショット。
二人は最後まで横並びのまま歩き続ける。カメラは女性の真横の位置を維持し、前後へ回り込まない。ズーム、寄り引き、構図変更なし。
女性は基本的に前を見て歩き、男性に話しかけるときだけ自然に隣を見る。男性を見るときは、少し見上げるようにカメラレンズを見る。
スマートフォンで歩きながら撮影したようなリアルな質感。軽い手ブレ、自然な上下動、小さなピントの迷い、わずかな露出変化。映画的に作り込みすぎない。
BGMなし。足音、風、遠くの車など自然な夜の環境音のみ。
女性は失恋した直後だが、大げさに悲しまず、仲のいい男友達に愚痴っている自然なテンション。
0〜30秒
二人は横並びのまま夜道を歩いている。
女「三年付き合って、別れるの五分だったんだけど！」
言い終わるあたりで、女性が隣の男性を少し見上げる。
男「五分？」
女「うん。こっちは昨日、全然寝れなかったのに」
女性は自然に前を見る。
男「……ほぉ」
少し間を置いて、
女「しかも最後に言われたの、『袋いる？』だよ。スーパーかよ」
「スーパーかよ」は、少し呆れながら自分でも笑ってしまうような自然な言い方。
男「袋もらった？」
女性が「そこ聞く？」というような表情で男性を見る。
女「もらった」
男「もらったんだ」
女性が少し笑う。
女「だって荷物あったし」
言い終わったあと、二人で小さく笑う。
女性はまた前を向き、そのまま二人で歩き続ける。
字幕、テロップ、ロゴ、ウォーターマークなし。
男性の姿、腕、手は映さない。
女性は手に何も持たない。
セリフ以外の不自然な口パクなし。

(extend)

前の映像からそのまま連続して始まる。30秒間ワンショット。男性と女性は最後まで完全に横並びで、同じ方向へ同じペースで歩き続ける。カメラの高さ、女性との距離、画角、位置関係は前半から変えない。男性は女性より少し背が高く、カメラは女性の真横からわずかに見下ろしている。女性の体は進行方向を向いたまま、男性を見るときだけ顔を向けて少し見上げるようにカメラレンズを見る。
女性が「だって荷物あったし」と言ったあとの小さな笑いが残っている。二人で少し笑い、そのまま数歩歩く。笑いが収まり、少し静かな空気になる。
女性は前を向いたまま、少し小さな声で、
女「……もっと何か言うと思ってた」
ぽろっと本音が出たような自然な言い方。
男「引き止めてほしかった？」
女性は少し考えながら前を向いたまま、
女「いや、別れるのは決めてたけど」
言い終わるあたりで少し男性を見る。
男「うん」
女性はまた前を見る。少し間を置いて、
女「……でも、なんかなぁ。なんかモヤるわぁ」
深刻に言いすぎず、自分でもうまく説明できない気持ちをそのまま話すような自然なトーン。
男「うむ」
女性は一瞬だけ男性を見て、少し「何その返事」という表情をするが何も言わず、また前を見る。
2〜3秒ほど会話が途切れる。足音、夜の風、遠くの車の音だけ。少し風が吹き、女性が肩をほんの少しすくめる。
女「なんか寒いな〜。 ひとりになったからかな〜？」
冗談っぽく、少し大げさに言う。「ひとりになったからかな〜？」と言いながら男性へ顔を向け、少し見上げるようにカメラレンズを見る。
男「あたためますか？」
男性は何でもないような自然な声で言う。ふざけた言い方にはしない。
このセリフは、前半の「袋いる？」→「スーパーかよ」という会話を男性が覚えていて、その流れを拾って女性を少し笑わせようとしているボケ。
女性はすぐには意図に気づかず、男性を見上げたまま一瞬だけ表情が止まる。約1秒〜1.5秒ほど間を置き、前半の「スーパーかよ」の流れを拾ったボケだと気づく。同時に、男性が自分の話をちゃんと聞いていて、重く慰めるのではなく笑わせようとしてくれていることにも自然に気づく。
その瞬間、女性の表情が少し柔らかくなる。大げさに感動せず、小さな嬉しさが表情ににじむ程度。
女「……コンビニかよ！」
怒ったツッコミではなく、「そこ拾ってくるんだ（笑）」という嬉しさと親しさが混じった言い方。最初の「……」はボケに気づくまでの一拍。「コンビニかよ！」と言うときには少し笑っている。
言い終わったあと、女性が少し下を向いて小さく笑う。男性もカメラの後ろから自然に少し笑う。女性はもう一度だけ男性をちらっと見上げ、少し嬉しそうな笑顔を残したまま前を向く。
「……コンビニかよ！」以降、新しいセリフは追加しない。そのまま二人で横並びに歩き続け、足音と夜の環境音だけを残して終了する。
演技は全体的に大げさにしない。「温めますか？」を恋愛的な意味に受け取る演技にはしない。すぐには意味が分からない → 前半のボケを拾ったことに気づく → 自分を笑わせようとしてくれた優しさにも気づく → 少し嬉しくなる → 「……コンビニかよ！」と笑って返す、という小さな感情変化で見せる。
恋愛感情を明確に出しすぎず、「この人、ちゃんと話聞いてくれてたんだ」「この人といると少し楽になるな」くらいの感情に留める。
カメラは最後まで女性の真横。女性が男性より前へ出ない。男性が女性より後ろへ下がらない。女性の正面へ回り込まない。振り返っているような構図にしない。カットなし、ズームなし、寄り引きなし、構図変更なし、カメラ位置変更なし。BGMなし。字幕、テロップ、ロゴ、ウォーターマーク、画面内文字なし。

DURATION: EXACTLY 10 SECONDS
ASPECT RATIO: 16:9
STYLE: Premium Hollywood live-action psychological horror, ultra-photorealistic humans, grounded CGI, realistic physics, elegant Japanese dark fantasy, desaturated cinematic photography. No anime rendering.

ENVIRONMENT
Vast abandoned underground Japanese temple. Aged wooden pillars, black stone flooring, shallow reflective water, old oil lanterns, faint moonlight and floor-level mist. Deep architectural layers create oppressive atmosphere and strong spatial depth.

LIGHTING / COLOR
Cold blue-gray moonlight, restrained amber lanterns, detailed shadows, subtle haze, realistic reflections, natural skin tones. Desaturated charcoal, black, gray, and weathered wood. No neon.

ACEN
Calm, composed, elegant, intimidating. Natural human performance. Zanpakutō remains physically consistent.

CORE CONCEPT
Kyōka Suigetsu manifests gradually:

EMPTY SPACE → SUBTLE DISTORTION → TRANSPARENT ACEN → INCREASING DENSITY → FULLY REALISTIC ACEN.

Approximately 12–14 manifestations emerge asynchronously across different depths and positions, never in formations. No instant appearance, teleportation, holograms or pop-in. Each has subtle, independent human movements.

ACTION / CAMERA

0.0–1.5s — ACTIVATION
Medium-wide shot. Camera slowly arcs around Acen as he draws his Zanpakutō. Cold light catches the blade. He quietly says “Kudakero, Kyōka Suigetsu.” Metallic blade sound and distant ambience only. No aura or explosion.

1.5–3.0s — FIRST MANIFESTATIONS
Camera continues moving. Empty space behind a pillar subtly distorts, gradually forming a transparent Acen. Three more emerge independently near a wall pillar, and water. Background remains visible through them. Subtle blinking and head movements.

3.0–5.0s — THE ROOM BEGINS TO FILL
Lateral tracking reveals additional Acens behind pillars and near the water. Some are faint, others 50–70% opaque and one nearly solid. Natural breathing, posture adjustments, and subtle sword-grip movements. No synchronization.

5.0–7.0s — COMPLETE HYPNOSIS ESCALATES
Camera passes foreground architecture, revealing 9–11 scattered manifestations across different depths. Some are partially hidden or visible through reflections. Skin, fabric, shadows, reflections and mist gradually respond like real physical bodies.

7.0–8.8s — REALITY BECOMES UNTRUSTWORTHY
Passing another pillar reveals 12–14 Acens throughout the sanctuary.Some are solid, some translucent others obscured. Every manifestation develops gradually from empty space. No attacks or theatrical reactions.

8.8–10.0s — FINAL REVEAL
Camera passes a final pillar, revealing a fully solid Acen close to the lens. No glow or distortion.He calmly looks toward the camera with a faint smile. Numerous manifestations remain scattered behind him in different states of solidity.The original is indistinguishable.CUT TO BLACK.

CAMERA LANGUAGE
Continuous lateral tracking with a subtle orbital arc. Use pillars darkness, and parallax to reveal manifestations naturally. Maintain spatial depth. No frantic handheld random shake, or unnecessary cuts.

VFX / PHYSICS:Grounded CGI, realistic human integration, progressive solidity, consistent shadows and reflections natural fabric movement, mist displacement and water interaction. No holograms, glowing edges particles, dissolves or teleportation.

PERFORMANCEAcen remains unnervingly calm. No screaming, exaggerated expressions, attacks, or unnecessary sword choreography. Horror comes from numerous realistic versions occupying the sanctuary.

NEGATIVE: Anime, cartoon, videogame render plastic skin, holograms, clone formations synchronized movements, static mannequins, instant materialization teleportation, magical explosions, neon, distorted anatomy duplicated limbs, floating sword inconsistent reflections or shadows rubber physics excessive camera shake chaotic editing cheap horror oversaturated colors.

text: Create a 15-second photorealistic, heartwarming animal story in one continuous shot. Maintain natural animal movement, realistic fur, believable object contact, and readable action.Set the sequence on one sheltered garden veranda during a bright, chilly afternoon. text:
Create a 15-second cinematic cooking sequence, 16:9 landscape, using the two supplied reference images.

REFERENCE CONSISTENCY
Reference Image 1 defines the single character: preserve the exact black-and-red armor, helmet, mechanical dreadlock tubes, visible eyes, armored hands, proportions, materials, and surface details. The character wears the gas mask while cooking. Only the gas mask is removed before eating; the helmet, tubes, and body armor remain unchanged. Keep all weapons secured and inactive.
Reference Image 2 defines the kitchen: preserve its black marble island, dark wood cabinetry, warm amber lighting, pendant lamps, appliances, and spatial layout.

Treat both reference sheets as design references. Render a full-screen cinematic scene with one character, not the diagrams, multiple views, labels, or panels.

CONCEPT AND VISUAL STYLE
A formidable armored character expertly prepares an irresistibly appetizing Japanese hamburger steak topped with a sunny-side-up egg and glossy brown demi-glace sauce, then removes the gas mask and enjoys the meal alone.

Use realistic cinematic materials, warm highlights on black metal, delicate steam, a deeply browned meat crust, glossy sauce, and a rich golden egg yolk. Serve one hamburger steak and one fried egg on a white ceramic plate.
DIRECTING
Use action-film camera language: fast low-angle tracking, precise whip pans, short orbital moves, motivated push-ins, and action-matched cuts. Let the camera follow the hands, utensils, and food. Finish each fast move with a clear, readable composition.

Use a brisk cooking montage during the first eight seconds, followed by controlled camera movement for mask removal and eating. Compress actual cooking time through editorial cuts. The hamburger steak is fully cooked before plating; the egg white is set while the yolk remains runny.

The timestamps below describe consecutive one-second action beats. Preserve the order and allocate enough time for the physical mask removal and the final bite.
SECOND-BY-SECOND SEQUENCE

00:00–00:01
An armored hand lowers a thick hamburger steak into a hot skillet with a spatula. It immediately sizzles. Begin at skillet-rim height with a fast lateral dolly toward the point of contact. Tiny oil droplets and steam catch the warm kitchen light.

00:01–00:02
CUT FORWARD IN COOKING TIME. The character smoothly flips the steak once with the spatula, revealing a beautifully browned crust. The camera follows the turn in a tight upward arc, then settles as the steak lands firmly in the pan.

00:02–00:03
CUT to both armored hands cracking one egg over a second skillet. A quick whip pan follows the forearm and resolves into a steady close-up as the shell opens and the egg drops into the pan. Keep the yolk whole.

00:03–00:04
Continue the egg shot. The camera makes a short, low macro slide beside the pan as the egg white begins sizzling around the domed golden yolk. Emphasize delicate bubbles and the clean, glossy yolk surface.
00:04–00:05
CUT FORWARD IN COOKING TIME to the browned hamburger steak. The character pours a small stream of thick demi-glace sauce around it. A fast push-in follows the stream down to the bubbling sauce, ending on the glistening meat.

00:05–00:06
The character lifts the cooked steak with a spatula and transfers it onto the white plate immediately beside the skillet. The camera tracks the short movement horizontally, keeping the steak sharp as sauce clings to its surface.
00:06–00:07
CUT to the cooked sunny-side-up egg being lifted from the second skillet. The camera follows the spatula in a tight descending movement as the character gently slides the egg onto the center of the steak. The yolk remains intact.

00:07–00:08
The character slides the completed plate a short distance into its dining position on the island. A brisk 30-degree camera orbit reveals the imposing masked character behind the steaming food. End with the golden yolk prominent in the foreground.
00:08–00:09
CUT to the character seated alone at the island. Both hands release the gas mask’s side catches. Begin a controlled push-in from a three-quarter angle. Clearly show the hands gripping the mask while it still covers the face.

00:09–00:10
Continue without cutting. The character physically pulls the gas mask forward, away from the face, then lowers it. Reveal the mouth naturally while preserving the same visible eye region and skin tone. The helmet and mechanical dreadlock tubes remain completely unchanged.
00:10–00:11
Continue the same action. The character places the removed mask on the countertop to the right of the plate. The camera tilts down with the hand, clearly showing the mask touch the surface and remain there as a solid object.

00:11–00:12
CUT to a low close-up of the plate. Using a fork and table knife, the character cuts through the egg and cooked hamburger steak. The camera makes a short push-in as golden yolk flows over the browned meat and blends with the glossy sauce. Show a moist, fully cooked interior.
00:12–00:13
Continue the food shot. The fork lifts one small bite coated with yolk and sauce. The camera rises smoothly with the fork, maintaining sharp focus on the appetizing bite and its delicate steam.

00:13–00:14
CUT to a three-quarter facial close-up. The character brings the fork to the exposed mouth, takes the bite, and begins chewing naturally. Use a gentle forward camera drift. The gas mask remains on the countertop.
00:14–00:15
Continue without cutting. The character’s eyes soften with quiet satisfaction and the shoulders relax slightly. Make a small, smooth dolly backward to include the steaming plate and warm kitchen surroundings. End on the character peacefully enjoying the meal alone.

SOUND
No background music, narration, or dialogue.
Use synchronized cooking and environmental sounds: strong sizzling, an egg cracking, sauce bubbling, subtle armor movement, spatula contact, mask catches clicking, the mask touching the countertop, and quiet cutlery sounds. Let the intense cooking sounds transition into calm kitchen ambience during the final seconds.
CONTINUITY AND QUALITY
Exactly one character, one hamburger steak, and one fried egg.
Maintain consistent hands, utensils, armor, kitchen geometry, and food placement.
The gas mask stays on during cooking, is physically removed at 00:09–00:10, and remains beside the plate afterward.
Use ordinary kitchen utensils for cooking.
Keep food and hand movements readable despite the energetic camera.
Avoid duplicated fingers, floating utensils, teleporting ingredients, changing faces, dissolving masks, extra people, explosive flames, excessive camera shake, subtitles, captions, and reference-sheet text.

author: @Zyvex_0x
text:
Create a 15-second vertical 9:16 video. Real raw smartphone footage of a real prank inside an elevator of an ordinary residential apartment building. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermark, no music. It must look exactly like a real viral prank clip filmed on a phone by friends, not a movie, not CGI, not acted.

CAMERA
A smartphone is hidden high in the top front corner of the elevator cabin, just under the ceiling, right above the door on the LEFT side. It looks steeply down and diagonally into the cabin toward the back wall. The lens is a wide phone lens with mild natural barrel distortion at the edges, no fisheye. The camera is completely fixed for the whole video: no shake, no zoom, no pan. From this angle the viewer sees almost the whole floor, the mirror back wall with the handrail, the right side wall, and on the left edge of the frame the open doorway and a strip of the landing outside. The man is visible head to sneakers at every moment, seen from above and slightly from behind when he faces the back wall.

IMAGE QUALITY
Real smartphone video indoors: cool white light from a flat LED ceiling panel mixed with warmer light from the stairwell outside, slightly saturated colours like a typical viral clip, light digital noise in the darker corners, natural sharpness, the landing outside a bit overexposed. Natural motion blur only on the fastest moments (the jump, the release, the fall) and the image is sharp again right after. Skin, fabric and steel look real. No smearing, no ghosting, no melting shapes, no plastic skin, no beauty filter, no cinematic lighting, no slow motion.

LOCATION
A narrow passenger elevator in a modern residential apartment block, about 1.1 metres wide and 1.4 metres deep. The back wall is one large mirror in a brushed steel frame. A round horizontal brushed steel handrail runs across the full width of the back wall, at about hip height, mounted on two short brackets, about 5 cm away from the mirror. The left and right side walls are brushed stainless steel panels with fine vertical grain, a few scratches and fingerprints. On the right wall near the door: a steel button panel with round buttons and a small white paper notice taped above it. The ceiling is a flat white LED light panel. The steel sliding doors are fully open the whole video and never move. Outside the doors: an apartment building landing with light grey stone tiles, a white wall, a brown apartment door with a metal number plate, a radiator under a window with daylight. Nobody is on the landing.

THE MIRROR
The back mirror reflects the man and the cabin naturally, from the opposite side, matching his movements exactly. The camera itself is never visible in the mirror. The reflection never moves on its own.

THE FLOOR ILLUSION (make it terrifying)
The entire cabin floor, wall to wall and right up to the door threshold, is covered by one flat printed vinyl floor sticker. The print is a sharp, ultra realistic photo shot straight down an endless elevator shaft in an old high-rise: two rusty steel guide rails and thick greasy black cables running down into pitch black darkness, stained wet concrete walls with cracks, rows of closed shaft doors of lower floors getting smaller and smaller, metal crossbeams, a few dim orange work lights far below fading into darkness, dust in the air. The perspective goes down at least 30 floors, so the drop looks bottomless and deadly. At the very bottom, tiny and far away, a broken elevator car roof is barely visible in the dark. From the camera angle and from the doorway it looks completely real: as if there is no floor and stepping in means falling to death. The print is matte, does not glow, has no reflections. The sticker lies perfectly flat and its edges are tight against the walls and invisible until 00:11. Under it is a plain dark grey rubber elevator floor with small square anti-slip texture.

CHARACTER
One man, about 28 years old, clearly an adult. Stocky, strong, a little heavy, broad shoulders, thick arms. Short curly dark brown hair, a short dark beard, light olive skin, a small tattoo on his left forearm. He wears an oversized washed black cotton t-shirt, grey cotton jogger shorts above the knee, white socks and white sneakers, a small dark grey crossbody bag on a strap across his chest. Wireless earbuds in his ears. He looks like an ordinary guy coming home, not a model, not an actor. Real skin texture, real pores, natural face. His face, hair, beard, tattoo, clothes and bag stay exactly the same in every frame.

ACTING STYLE
He does not act. Every reaction is real, instant, instinctive and clumsy, like a real person who truly believes there is a deadly drop under his feet. Nothing is choreographed, graceful or symmetrical. Real body weight: he jumps heavily, hangs with straining arms, falls hard. Loud real breathing. He never looks at the camera until the last two seconds.

TIMELINE (the most important part, follow every detail)

00:00.0 - 00:00.3
The video starts with him already entering the elevator: he is mid-stride in the open doorway, his body already leaning into the cabin, walking fast and relaxed, looking at the mirror ahead, bag bouncing on his chest. His LEFT foot stands on the steel door threshold strip. His RIGHT foot is already swinging forward inside the cabin, in the air about 20 cm above the floor sticker, about to step down, but it never touches the floor.

00:00.3 - 00:00.5
Right before his RIGHT foot lands, his eyes drop and he sees the bottomless shaft directly under it. His whole body jolts in shock, both arms fly up, eyes huge, and he lets out a loud piercing scream: "AAAH!" His RIGHT foot stays in the air and jerks up toward his chest instead of stepping down.

00:00.5 - 00:00.9
Still screaming, with the RIGHT knee already pulled up, he pushes off hard from the threshold with his LEFT foot and throws himself forward into the cabin toward the back wall, both arms reaching for the handrail, both feet in the air, knees pulling up, flying over the "shaft". His sneakers never touch the elevator floor at any moment.

00:00.9 - 00:01.3
Mid-air he slams into the back wall: both hands grab the handrail from above, fingers wrapped tight around it, his chest almost touching the mirror. His knees yank up to his chest and both sneakers slam against the bottom of the mirror and the lower steel frame below the rail.

00:01.3 - 00:02.0
He settles into a tight terrified crouch hanging on the rail: facing the mirror, back to the camera, elbows bent and raised high, both hands gripping the rail, head pulled into his shoulders, knees tucked against his chest, sneakers pressed flat against the bottom of the mirror and the left and right corners. His butt sticks out over the "shaft". His whole weight is held by his arms on the rail and his feet on the wall. In the mirror we see his face: pale, eyes wide, mouth open.

00:02.0 - 00:04.0
He hangs there like a frozen scared spider, shaking. His arms tremble, his legs tremble. He keeps looking down over his shoulder at the shaft, then back at the mirror, breathing in short loud gasps. He whimpers in a high cracking voice: "No no no no no!" His sneakers squeak as they slip a little on the mirror and he pushes them back.

00:04.0 - 00:04.8
A quick cut: the camera shows a straight-down view of the sticker filling the whole frame, the endless dark shaft looking totally real, as if we are falling with him. Then cut back to the same corner camera.

00:04.8 - 00:06.5
Back in the corner view, he is still hanging, now in full panic: he shifts his grip one hand at a time, his body twisting left and right, his t-shirt riding up, the bag swinging under him. He looks toward the open door to his left, realizing it is the only way out.

00:06.5 - 00:08.0
He tries to climb toward the door: he slides his hands along the rail to the LEFT end, then pushes his LEFT sneaker against the left side wall next to the door frame and his RIGHT sneaker against the back corner, legs spreading wide into a shaky split over the shaft, crotch low, knees bent, thighs shaking. He is almost there, his left foot touching the door frame. He grunts loudly with effort.

00:08.0 - 00:08.5
He lets go of the rail with his RIGHT hand and swings it back and to the left, reaching for the door frame behind him. His body twists open, his weight shifts backward. His left hand is now the only grip.

00:08.5 - 00:08.9
His left hand slips off the rail. Both feet slip off the walls. He tips backward into the air with arms flailing and legs kicking up.

00:08.9 - 00:09.4
He falls backward and lands hard on his back on the floor with a heavy thud, head toward the door and the camera, legs flying straight up in the air, sneakers pointing at the ceiling. He screams loudly the whole fall: "AAAAAH!" His mouth is wide open, eyes squeezed shut.

00:09.4 - 00:10.2
His legs bounce and drop. He lies on his back, arms spread, still screaming, then the scream breaks into gasping. His body is curled, knees up, hands clawing at the floor, waiting to fall into the shaft.

00:10.2 - 00:11.0
Nothing happens. He freezes. He opens his eyes, rolls a little onto his side, and slaps the floor with his right palm twice, feeling it. It is solid. His face turns from terror to confusion.

00:11.0 - 00:11.6
He spots the edge of the sticker where it meets the right wall. His fingers scratch at it, catch the corner and lift it. The vinyl peels up with a sharp ripping sound, showing the plain grey rubber floor underneath.

00:11.6 - 00:12.6
He scrambles onto his knees and rips the sticker up with both hands in one big angry pull, tearing it off the floor, the whole shaft image bending and crumpling in his hands, the normal grey elevator floor appearing under him.

00:12.6 - 00:13.2
He jumps to his feet and throws the crumpled sticker out of the open doors onto the landing tiles.

00:13.2 - 00:15.0
He spins around, looks straight up into the camera in the corner, and screams at it in pure rage, red faced, arms spread wide, stomping one foot: "WHO DID THIS?! ARE YOU SERIOUS?!" Loud laughter from his friends echoes from the stairwell off screen. The video ends on him still yelling at the camera.

BODY AND PHYSICS RULES
He always has exactly two arms, two legs and two hands with five fingers each. Joints bend only in natural directions. At every moment his weight is supported by something real: his feet on the floor, his hands on the rail together with his feet on the walls, or his body on the floor. He never floats, never hovers, never sticks to a wall without holding the rail, never turns upside down, never walks on walls or the ceiling. His hands never merge with the rail, the bag or the sticker. The rail never bends or moves. The floor is always solid and flat, he never sinks or falls through it. Clothes and bag move with gravity and inertia. Before the fall at 00:08.9 his feet never touch the cabin floor: he jumps directly from the door threshold onto the handrail.

OBJECTS
One handrail on the back wall. One mirror. One button panel. One paper notice. One crossbody bag, always on its strap across his chest. One floor sticker: flat until 00:11, then peeled and ripped up in one piece and thrown out at 00:13. No other objects appear, nothing duplicates, vanishes or changes shape. No readable text anywhere.

CONTINUITY
Same man, same face, same clothes, same lighting, same corner camera angle for the whole video, except the single short straight-down shaft shot at 00:04.0 - 00:04.8. The doors stay open. Only one person is ever visible. The camera is never seen in the mirror. The background never warps.

SOUND
Real phone audio, slightly echoey in the small steel cabin: fast footsteps, the elevator ventilation hum, his sharp gasp, his loud scream as he jumps from the doorway, sneaker squeaks on the mirror, his whimpering "no no no", grunts and heavy breathing, a long loud scream during the fall, a heavy thud on landing, the loud ripping of vinyl, his furious yelling at the camera, and friends bursting out laughing in the stairwell.

FINAL FEEL
A raw, real, hilarious prank clip that looks completely genuine: a real guy, real panic, real fall, real anger. Not acted, not polished, not CGI.

Kling 4.0 Prompt:

[Shot 1 - 3.5s] Low tracking shot pulling backward fast. Foreground: tumbling stone masonry and jagged bridge chains slicing the frame. Subject: The knight sprints at full speed toward the lens, leaping over a gaping chasm in the flagstones as their cape whips in high winds. Background: crumbling bridge parapets dissolving into storm clouds. The camera runs backward ahead of the knight with heavy, kinetic handheld shake. Cut on the knight planting both boots to slide.

[Shot 2 - 3.0s] Low worm's-eye upward angle. Foreground: shattered balustrades exploding outward. Subject: The titanic front leg of the iron colossus crashes down into the bridge deck, obliterating a stone watchtower into flying shrapnel. Background: the colossal underbelly of the machine spewing embers into the sky. Violent arcs of black lightning flash across the stormy sky on the upper right, casting rapid, high-contrast strobing chiaroscuro shadows across wet granite and pitted iron. The camera whips upward violently, tracking the impact shockwave. Cut on falling granite blocks.

[Shot 3 - 2.5s] Extreme close-up. Foreground: the heavy iron string of the Greatbow vibrating under extreme tension. Subject: The knight draws a massive jagged metal arrow to their ear; black lightning coils around the arrow tip, illuminating the knight's visor slits in blinding white light. Background: blurred storm clouds rushing past. Violent arcs of black lightning flash across the stormy sky on the upper right, casting rapid, high-contrast strobing chiaroscuro shadows across wet granite and pitted iron. The camera pushes in fast on the drawing gauntlet. Cut on the string releasing.

[Shot 4 - 4.0s] Profile tracking shot. Foreground: masonry ripping up from the floor. Subject: The colossal Great-arrow streaks across the bridge wrapped in a cone of displaced air and black electrical discharge, heading straight for the titan's glowing chest vent. Background: the looming silhouette of the colossus. Violent arcs of black lightning flash across the stormy sky on the upper right, casting rapid, high-contrast strobing chiaroscuro shadows across wet granite and pitted iron. The camera tracks laterally alongside the projectile at high speed. Cut on explosive contact.

[Shot 5 - 8.0s] Wide low-angle reaction shot. Foreground: the knight sliding to one knee, bracing the unstrung bow. Subject: The arrow pierces the colossus’s molten exhaust core; an internal secondary explosion erupts in blinding silver sparks, forcing the titanic beast to stumble backward onto its hind legs with a deafening metallic screech. Background: shattered fortress spires in the distance. Violent arcs of black lightning flash across the stormy sky on the upper right, casting rapid, high-contrast strobing chiaroscuro shadows across wet granite and pitted iron. The camera cranes rapidly upward and tilts down, capturing the massive machine rocking off-balance. Cut on severed cables snapping.

text:
SCENE: three places in one continuous bare-handed fight, each change of place triggered by a body crashing through something: an apartment corridor, then the cramped entrance hall of an apartment full of scattered shoes, then a concrete outdoor stairwell high above the street.
CAST: two women, one in a plain grey sweatshirt, the other in a plain navy sweatshirt.
CAMERA:
- Corridor (0-4s): over the grey fighter's shoulder as the navy fighter rushes her with a flurry of punches, fluorescent white light, apartment doors flashing past.
- The grey fighter's back slams through a half-open apartment door; the camera whip-pans with the impact, the motion blur carrying us into the entrance hall.
- Entrance hall (4-8s): three fast angle changes, one from floor level among the shoes, as they wrestle; the door chain swinging; a shoe spinning through the air past the lens. Warm yellow bulb light.
- A focus pull from the swinging door chain in the foreground to the navy fighter's face as she catches her breath for half a second.
- The camera pushes straight through a hanging coat on the coat hook as both women tumble through a second door onto the outdoor stairwell.
- Stairwell (10-15s): grey daylight, wind, the street far below; the camera drops from above as they fight down the stairs, then a crash zoom on the final throw.
MOTION RULES:
- Every place change happens exactly on an impact; the world gets bigger with each one: a door, then a wall of shoes and coats, then open sky.
- In the corridor the rush runs at five strikes per second; in the entrance hall it becomes grappling and elbows in the tight space; on the stairwell it becomes leaps from landing to landing.
- The navy fighter leaps down a whole flight of stairs feet-first; the grey fighter sidesteps, pivots 180 degrees mid-sprint and suplexes her onto the landing: the single maximum hit, one-third speed for half a second, the railing shuddering, dust blasting off the concrete.
- The grey fighter starts laughing in the middle of the fight and her strength drains for a moment; the navy fighter gains the upper hand until the suplex turns it back.
Impacts come in three tiers. Normal hits: a two-frame hold, a jump in brightness, a two-to-four-frame camera jolt, sleeves and hair trailing 0.1 seconds behind. Heavy hits: a three-frame dead stop, then sweat, dust or water bursts radially from the contact point, a six-frame hard shake, the struck body carried by momentum, fabric settling 0.4 seconds later. One maximum hit only: the whole frame flashes toward white, radial blur spreads from the contact point, and the surroundings break.
